elaine: Heads up 1: product asked if we can offer bounded-latency writes for EU tenants while keeping strict residency. they want 'local write' experience in NA but data must remain in EU. can we support dual-write without breaking residency?
bhavik: Short answer: only if both write endpoints are in-residency or if NA acts as a forwarder/proxy. true active-active with writes in NA would violate residency unless we rewrap/keep material in EU KMS and never store plaintext in NA.
nate: Two pragmatic paths: 1) EU-primary lease + NA-forward (sync or async) 2) true dual-region active-active but encrypt using EU-only key material and NA holds only opaque ciphertext + proof. 2 is complex (cross-region KMS wrapping) and has operational risk for KMS availability.
tara: For (2) we need a clear KMS contract: whenever a write would generate new encrypted material, the EU KMS must wrap it and return a wrapped blob that can be stored anywhere. If EU KMS p95>threshold, we must fail-write or switch tenant to forwarding mode. ops-bot: INCIDENT: eu-kms p95=1.9s right now.
bhavik: typo :)
bhavik: also: arbitration on conflicting writes. we should avoid app-layer merges where possible. propose a compact arbitration token attached to each write: {lease_epoch, origin, write_nonce}. server picks winner by (lease_epoch desc, origin priority) and returns conflict metadata so client can retry/merge.
ate: add a client-visible 409 with `merge_hint` payload if we detect causality violation and can't auto-resolve. many clients will handle 409+merge-hint. otherwise default to epoch_wins to keep it simple.
ara: that's tara not ara :)
tara: :smile: telemetry we need: conflicts, lease_contests, kms_wrap_errors, cross_region_forward_latency. also require an operator toggle to force-forwarding mode per-tenant.
ate: rollout plan: alpha with lease-first + read-steering | beta add NA-forwarding (sync straight-through) | gamma experiment with wrapped-active-active for selected tenants (legal signoff).
bhavik: implementation note: wrapped-active-active requires adding `wrap_metadata` with `region_origin` and `wrap_signature` (signed by EU KMS) so receivers can verify provenance without unwrapping. also rotation: keep per-region DEKs but maintain a canonical EU-wrapped envelope.
ate: failure scenarios: if EU KMS is down during a write, we must either retry, fail, or buffer. product prefers low-latency ack in NA; ops prefers correctness. opt-in per-tenant setting `prefer_availability` vs `prefer_residency_strict`.
ops-bot: deploybot: kicked off chaos test `kms-latency-spike` for eu-kms 30s. results in #eng-sre soon.
elaine: action items: nate document tenant opt-in flags and rollback semantics; bhavik draft arbitration token + response shapes; tara add telemetry events; runbook owners: nate+tana for KMS failure. schedule design review Fri 11am.
elaine: one more: require audit trail for any cross-region-forward: pre-write checksum, wrapped blob id, and post-apply confirmation. must be queryable by compliance.
ops-bot: noted: audit-log entry created for write-probe test id=writeprobe-5151.
elaine: thanks all, good start. we'll keep the design lightweight and prefer forwarding/lease-first as default.
